differentialResults.existingCases: All nine existing deterministic test bodies ported into owned test harness; same scenario outcomes against actual saved pre-reorder baseline and captured current production. Source code loaded from actual artifacts, not reconstructed baseline.
differentialResults.additionalCases: Queued versus delivered removals; detach/reattach on either side of scan; body/root replacement; metadata observer cleanup; dynamic=false consent; removal during dynamic-observer write-disconnection interval; pending cancel/failure/invalid reply/reconnect/restart; undefined WeakRefs; static and churn counts.
differentialResults.interpretation: 17 passing assertions per run include two expected rejection assertions. This is NOT full baseline equivalence or candidate acceptance.

steps: Adopt node 0 into a different connected document; deliver original document removal.
Run batch 2 sweep. node.isConnected is true, so both implementations keep the record.
Detach node 0 in the other document. Original document observer cannot observe this removal.
Run batch 3 sweep while node is disconnected. Baseline deletes the record; candidate skips sweep.
Reattach node to original document and Restore.

differentialResults.undefinedAfterEscape: After adoption and later foreign removal, forcing fake WeakRef undefined leads to 64 baseline dereferences versus 0 candidate dereferences at next boundary; skipped sweep cannot remove the stale WeakRef.

review.authoredCode: Candidate and complete 384-line owned harness fully read, including instrumentation, observer queue routing, cleanup, differential assertions and operation counters; exact hashes and line ranges are in files.
review.candidateMechanism: Separate active-run Document childList/subtree observer reduces records immediately to one boolean. takeRecords consumed at exact original per-batch sweep point. Original !node?.isConnected removal condition unchanged. Dynamic translation observer, scheduling, eligibility and all safety/size limits unchanged. Metadata observer stays connected during dynamic write disconnections and disconnects/resets on stop.
review.blockingFinding: A connected translated node can leave the observed Document through adoption. The first sweep must keep it by original isConnected semantics. Subsequent disconnected/collected state outside the observer domain is unobservable to the boolean. This produces a deterministic Restore regression in the fake model.
review.retention: No candidate callback stores records, removed nodes or DOM arrays. Browser MutationObserver itself may temporarily retain queued MutationRecords and removed subtrees until callback/takeRecords/disconnect. This is a new transient retention cost, unmeasured. The fixture intentionally owns nodes and fake WeakRefs strongly, so it cannot establish real collection or retention.
review.observability: No candidate source counters or global testing hooks. Sweep counters are injected only into VM code copies. Observable text/status/batch/listener/timer snapshots are compared. No claim to preserve all real-DOM observability.

limitations: Fake observer models explicit record queues, takeRecords/disconnect consumption and chosen callback checkpoints. It does not implement a browser event loop, transient registered observers, nested ancestry, shadow DOM or true TreeWalker root replacement semantics.
Body/root tests model removal coverage and Restore outcome only, not complete root-replacement traversal acceptance.

Mutation churn count is a finite 20-boundary fixture with 20 removals/reattachments each. Dirty boolean coalesces them to one sweep per boundary. Under removal at every boundary worst case remains quadratic, as required by baseline semantics.
Real MutationObserver record generation and transient allocation costs have not been measured.
Current and saved baseline hashes were verified from bytes; older shared reports were treated as input evidence, not current verification.
